Implementation Plan

## Implementation plan: security-pass fix cycle 2 for #7126 (`security-pass-fix-cycle-2`)

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `a04c8e7d809d0bf8c9b11d30fdb67df5a0b12625`, branch `orchestrator/project-7126` (integration branch metadata matches; mismatch = false).

Scope-mode: Selective Expansion
Reuse-audit: extends run_security_pass_inline
Scope-mode justification: Both findings describe code that is already fixed on `orchestrator/project-7126`. On this ref, `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` already does each of these:
- The open-PR list at line 27721 requests `isCrossRepository,headRepositoryOwner`, and forks are skipped at line 28131.
- Warnings and editor summaries are filtered on `user.login == UNBLOCK_TRUSTED_LOGIN` (lines 28200-28258 and 28399-28402), and an unresolved login skips the PR (line 28196).
- Gate C requires the pipeline git identity plus a push by the pipeline login, read from the repository activity API (lines 28449-28505).
- Gate D calls `_pr_wait_for_required_checks "${N_PR}" "${N_HEAD_SHA}" "${N_BASE_REF}" 0`. It fails closed on `helper_unavailable`, `no_check_runs` and pending checks.
- The merge passes `--match-head-commit "${N_HEAD_SHA}"` (line 28622).

`tests/test_orchestrate_poll_noop_suspicious_recovery.py` (lines 1012-1189) has behavioural tests for each of these.

The audit still reported them because of how the security pass prepares its checkout. With `keep_trusted_support=true`, `prepare_tracking_judge_checkout` calls `_judge_refresh_trusted_support` (lines 5649-5716). That overwrites every working-tree file under `scripts/` and `prompts/` with the verified support copy from `main` (`.codex-workflow-src`). `security_audit.sh` then runs from that checkout. `codex_isolated_workspace.snapshot_readonly` (lines 261-292) copies working-tree bytes of the tracked files, and the poller is 1.55 MB, under the 2 MiB cap, so it is snapshotted that way. The model therefore read `main`'s pre-fix `orchestrate_poll_process.sh` next to the branch's `changelog.d` fragment and the branch's git diff hunks. That is exactly the contradiction the finding states ("Not fixed at HEAD, although changelog.d/7126 says it is"), and it explains why the cited line numbers (27686, 28294, 28388) do not match this ref.

Two consequences follow:
- Every cycle will report the same false positives until the budget is exhausted.
- More importantly, the pass never audits a project's real changes to `scripts/` or `prompts/`, so a branch-added defect there passes unseen. That is a security false negative.

Changing the noop sweep again would not clear this finding. The root-cause fix is to audit a clean tree of the integration head while still running only trusted support code. It is small: one function, using existing mechanisms. By the Boil the Lake rule and §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > …), the complete fix is the right choice.

Assumption (encode as a code comment): the findings are already fixed in code at this head. The deliverable is the audit-tree fix plus regression tests that pin each control the finding names, so the next re-audit sees the real code. If a re-audit on a clean tree still reports a gap, it will be a real one.

## Functions or modules to implement

### 1. `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`: new helper `_security_pass_prepare_audit_tree`, plus a removal companion `_security_pass_remove_audit_tree`
Before adding them, check that neither name exists in the file (§10 uniqueness).

**Prepare.** Inputs are the head SHA and the tracking number.
- Resolve `RUNTIME_DIR` to an absolute path with `cd … && pwd -P`, and fail if that is not possible.
- Create `mktemp -d "${RUNTIME_DIR}/security-audit-tree.XXXXXX"`.
- Run `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null worktree add --quiet --detach "<dir>/tree" "<head_sha>"`.
- Verify `git -C <tree> rev-parse HEAD` equals the head SHA, and that `git -C <tree> status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` is empty.
- On success, print the tree path. On failure, remove what was created and return 1.

This follows the existing poller pattern `git worktree add --detach "${judge_wt}" …` (around line 9672).

**Remove.** Run `git worktree remove --force <tree>`, then `rm -rf <dir>` and `git worktree prune`. Failures warn only and never change the security verdict.

**Log line.** Add a new stable prefix: `SECURITY_PASS_AUDIT_TREE tracking_issue=<N> head_sha=<sha> outcome=prepared|failed|removed|remove_failed reason=<worktree_add_failed|head_mismatch|dirty_tree|runtime_dir_unavailable>`.

### 2. `run_security_pass_inline` (around lines 8131-8150)
**Trusted support root.** Right after the existing required-asset loop, which already checks that the trusted copies are present in the refreshed checkout, capture `security_pass_support_root="$(pwd -P)"`. That checkout's `scripts/` and `prompts/` are the verified support copies installed by `_judge_refresh_trusted_support`. Comment this: the checkout is trusted for execution only, and its working tree is never what gets audited.

**Audit tree.** Before `write_codex_config.sh`, call `_security_pass_prepare_audit_tree "${current_head_sha}"`. On failure, call `security_pass_fail_closed "engine_unavailable" "The integration head could not be checked out into a clean audit tree." "${prior_security_status}"` and return 1. This is the same fail-closed path as the other preparation failures.

**Audit invocation.** Replace the current invocation with a subshell, `( cd "${audit_tree}" || exit 97; <same env prefix> … )`, that:
- Keeps every existing `SECURITY_AUDIT_*`, `WORKFLOW_EDITOR_MODEL` and `AI_ENGINE_LABELS` assignment.
- Adds `SECURITY_AUDIT_SUPPORT_DIR="${security_pass_support_root}"`. This is the existing consumer staging path in `security_audit.sh` (line 496), so the prompt, `ai_engine.sh`, `codex_isolated_exec.sh` and the label helpers resolve from trusted support.
- Adds `SECURITY_AUDIT_FP_EXCLUSIONS="${security_pass_support_root}/scripts/security_audit_fp_exclusions.json"` as an absolute path. Without it, `security_audit.sh` lines 497-504 would prefer the audited tree's catalog, and a branch could suppress its own findings.
- Runs `bash "${security_pass_support_root}/scripts/codex_heartbeat.sh" … -- bash "${security_pass_support_root}/scripts/security_audit.sh" "${context_file}"`.

The subshell's return code is captured. The tree is removed right after, on success and failure alike. Only then is the rc evaluated with the same `security_pass_fail_closed "engine_unavailable" …` branch as today.

**Unchanged.** `security_audit.sh` itself does `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"`, which is now the audit tree. Its snapshot, synthetic `.git`, oversized-file chunks, diff scope (`git diff` on the shared object store) and the Claude `claude_run … "${PWD}"` all therefore see the integration head's committed content. `write_codex_config.sh` stays as it is (it writes HOME config). The fix-cycle diff computation, the state writes and the findings validation (`jq` schema check) are unchanged.

### 3. Tests

**`tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`:**
- Extend the security-pass sandbox mock at line 1188 so that `SECURITY_AUDIT_CAPTURE` also records:
  - `cwd`, or `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`;
  - `SECURITY_AUDIT_SUPPORT_DIR`;
  - `SECURITY_AUDIT_FP_EXCLUSIONS`;
  - the bytes of a probe file under `scripts/` read from the cwd.
- New test, branch content is audited: the integration branch commits `scripts/probe.sh` with "branch", and `.codex-workflow-src/scripts/probe.sh` contains "trusted". Assert that the audit cwd is a different directory from the checkout, that `probe.sh` there reads "branch", that the executed `security_audit.sh` is the trusted copy, and that `SECURITY_AUDIT_FP_EXCLUSIONS` is the absolute trusted path. A branch `scripts/security_audit_fp_exclusions.json` with different content must not be the one passed.
- New test, failed worktree setup: when `git worktree add` fails (stub `git`, or a pre-existing path), assert `engine_unavailable`, a `SECURITY_PASS_AUDIT_TREE … outcome=failed` line, and that no audit ran.
- New test, cleanup: after both a successful audit and a failing one (`security_audit_exit_code != 0`), the audit tree is gone and `git worktree list` shows only the checkout.
- Update existing captures that assert exact environment keys, if any break.

**`tests/test_orchestrate_poll_noop_suspicious_recovery.py`:** add one static contract test that pins the exact controls the finding names:
- The `STANDALONE_PRS` `gh pr list --json` field list contains `isCrossRepository` and `headRepositoryOwner`.
- Every noop-warning and editor-summary `jq` selection within the sweep section includes `.user.login`.
- The Gate D call is `_pr_wait_for_required_checks "${N_PR}" "${N_HEAD_SHA}" "${N_BASE_REF}" 0`.
- The single force-merge call carries `--match-head-commit "${N_HEAD_SHA}"`.

Existing behavioural tests already cover these, but this test fails loudly if a future sync from `main` drops one of them.
